questions.stem: A field biologist's survey finds a tetrahedral molecule; how many lone pairs on the central atom?

options.text: One, because tetrahedral includes a lone pair.

questions.learningObjective: Identify nonpolar bond from EN difference
questions.stem: A field biologist's survey gives an EN difference of 0.1; how is the bond best classified?

options.text: Ionic, because any difference creates ions.
Polar covalent, because electrons shift.
Metallic, because the atoms are metals.
Nonpolar covalent, because the difference is tiny.

questions.explanation: An EN difference below 0.4 indicates a nonpolar covalent bond. A 0.1 difference means nearly equal sharing.

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.stem: A field biologist's survey examines CF4; is it polar?

options.text: Yes, because C-F bonds are very polar.
options.misconception: equates bond polarity with molecular polarity

options.text: No, because CF4 is ionic.
Yes, because fluorine is highly electronegative.
No, because tetrahedral symmetry cancels dipoles.

questions.explanation: CF4 is nonpolar because its tetrahedral symmetry cancels the four C-F dipoles. Bond polarity does not guarantee molecular polarity.
